newsitem.title: USA: NCAA-SHAMMGOD TO STAY AT PROVIDENCE, BILLUPS IN NBA DRAFT.
newsitem.headline: NCAA-SHAMMGOD TO STAY AT PROVIDENCE, BILLUPS IN NBA DRAFT.

text.p: Providence sophomore point guard God Shammgod, one of the keys to the Friars' run to the Final Eight in the NCAA Tournament, said Friday he plans on returning for his junior year.
Published reports had Shammgod forgoing his final two years of eligibility to enter the NBA draft. But Shammgod ended the speculation by releasing a two-sentence statement through the college.
"At the present time, I plan on returning to Providence College for my junior year. If there is a change in the future, I will make an announcement."
Shammgod helped Providence (24-12) reach the Southeast Region final as the Friars beat Marquette, Duke, and Chattanooga before falling to eventual national champion Arizona 96-92 in overtime.
Shammgod averaged 10.4 points and a team-leading 6.7 assists per game this past season.
Meanwhile, another sophomore guard announced he was heading into the NBA Draft. University of Colorado star Chauncey Billups became the 13th player to apply for early entry to the draft.
Among those who have already declared are Kentucky sophomore forward Ron Mercer, Cincinnati junior forward Danny Fortson and North Carolina high school star Tracy McGrady.

Billups was a first-team All-Big 12 conference selection and led the Buffaloes to their first NCAA Tournament berth in 28 years. He averaged 19.1 points and 4.8 assists per game and also led the team in three-point field goals and steals.
Colorado finished 22-10 this past season and beat Indiana in the first round of the NCAA Tournament before losing to North Carolina in the second round.
